# 2 Maccabees Chapter 6 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_006_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Not long afterward, the king sent an elderly Athenian official to force the Jews to abandon the laws of their ancestors and to stop living by the laws of God.

**2** He was also to defile the temple in Jerusalem and rededicate it to Olympian Zeus. The sanctuary on Mount Gerizim was to be rededicated to Zeus-the-Friend-of-Strangers — a title that apparently suited its worshipers just fine.

**3** What followed was a brutal and overwhelming catastrophe.

**4** The temple was flooded with pagan debauchery and orgies. Gentiles slept with prostitutes in the sacred precincts. Men had intercourse with women inside the holy courts. Things were brought in that the law strictly forbade.

**5** The altar was heaped with prohibited offerings — everything the law condemned.

**6** You could not keep the sabbath. You could not observe any of the ancient festivals. You could not even admit out loud that you were a Jew.

**7** Every month on the king's birthday, the Jews were dragged by force to eat from the pagan sacrifices. When the festival of Dionysus came around, they were marched in procession for the god, crowned with ivy wreaths.

**8** At the urging of Ptolemy, orders went out to the neighboring Greek cities to enforce the same policy against the Jews — to force them to participate in pagan sacrifices

**9** and to execute those who refused to convert to Greek ways. The full horror of the situation was clear for all to see.

**10** Two women were arrested for circumcising their babies. The authorities paraded them through the streets of the city with their infants tied to their breasts, then threw them off the city wall to their deaths.

**11** Another group had gathered secretly in nearby caves to observe the sabbath. They were betrayed. Philip came and burned them alive inside the caves. They refused to defend themselves, out of reverence for the sabbath's holiness.

**12** To those who read this book, I want to say something directly: do not let these horrors drive you to despair. These sufferings were not meant to destroy our people — they were meant to correct us.

**13** It is actually a sign of God's goodness that the wicked are punished quickly rather than left unchecked.

**14** With other nations, the Sovereign Lord is patient — he lets their sins accumulate to their full measure before he acts. With us, he has chosen a different way.

**15** He acts early, so that he will not be forced to punish us to the full extent of our sins later on.

**16** He never withdraws his mercy from us. He may discipline us through terrible events, but he never abandons his own people.

**17** That is enough by way of explanation. Now we must get back to the story.

**18** Eleazar was one of the most distinguished scholars of the law — an old man of noble bearing and great reputation. The authorities tried to force him to open his mouth and eat pork.

**19** He chose an honorable death over a defiled life. He walked up to the instrument of torture himself, spitting out the meat,

**20** as any person of real courage must do — someone who refuses to eat what the law forbids, even for the love of life.

**21** Some of the officials present had known Eleazar for many years. They took him aside privately and made him an offer: bring your own meat — kosher food — eat it openly, and pretend you have eaten the forbidden meat as the king ordered.

**22** This way, they said, you will escape with your life, and we will have shown you the consideration your old friendship with us deserves.

**23** But Eleazar made his choice. It was a choice worthy of everything he was: his years, his dignity, his magnificent white hair earned through a life well lived, his conduct from earliest childhood, and above all, the holy laws given by God. He answered them immediately: send me to Hades.

**24** "This kind of deception," he said, "is not fitting for a man my age. Imagine if the young men thought that Eleazar — at ninety years old — had converted to a foreign religion.

**25** What kind of example would that set? For the sake of a few more days of life, I would be corrupting them, and I would be smearing dishonor over everything my old age has stood for.

**26** Maybe I could escape human punishment by going through with it. But I cannot escape the hands of the Almighty — not alive, not dead.

**27** So by giving up my life bravely right now, I will prove I am worthy of the age I have reached.

**28** And I will leave something real behind for the young — a clear example of how to choose death over compromise, and how to die well for the laws that are sacred and holy."

**29** He finished speaking and went directly to the torture rack.

**30** The men who had tried to help him now turned against him. They thought what he had said was the raving of a madman.

**31** As the blows fell and death drew close, he cried out: "The LORD knows, in his holy knowledge, that I could have been spared. My body is in agony from these blows — but my soul is at peace in this suffering, because I am in awe of him."

**32** That is how he died. By his death he left not just an inspiring story but a living monument of nobility — not for the young only, but for the whole nation to remember.
